Recomputed from our own n_H, chi = 1.08, alpha_B(2e4 K) = 1.43e-13 cm^3/s.

checks.detail: zeta_gamma x t_rec = 0.0647 at z = 10. BELOW UNITY, which is the correct and expected answer: escaping stellar photons at this redshift cannot yet balance recombinations in ionized gas -- that is what it MEANS for reionization to be incomplete at z = 10. The Hubble-time form, zeta_gamma x t_H = 0.1039, differs from it by exactly t_rec/t_H = 0.6228. The two clocks DIVERGE with redshift: t_rec/t_H ~ (1+z)^-1.5 in matter domination, so the maintenance criterion gets HARDER at higher z, not easier.
checks.name: maintenance criterion in the STANDARD normalisation, zeta t_rec

checks.detail: keeping the IGM ionized needs 1 + t_H/t_rec = 2.61 ionizations per atom per Hubble time (MD14's 'close to two'); the stellar channel supplies 0.1039, short by a factor 25.1. Closing that gap is the job of the RISE of rho_SFR between z = 10 and z ~ 6, for which this document adopts no star-formation history -- so the shortfall is REPORTED, not explained away. This replaces the earlier claim that zeta_gamma t_H = 0.104 was 'the pace required for reionization to complete near z ~ 6'.
checks.name: how far short the z = 10 rate falls -- stated, not hidden
